newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares fall from heights, outlook unclear.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares fall from heights, outlook unclear.

text.p: Danish share prices closed only a little higher on Friday after falling from record intra-day heights earlier on, with dealers unsure about Monday's market, which they said would track Wall Street.
"Monday's market will depend very much on U.S. trends, it is impossible to say which way the index will go," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index hit an intra-day record of 168.62 point only to slip and finish the week 0.69 point higher at 168.14 in overall bourse turnover of 1.516 billion crowns. The KFX June future rose 0.65 point to 168.70 with 376 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Banks, Novo Nordisk and Tele Danmark helped the index up, with BG Bank closing 10 crowns higher at 320 on a NatWest buy recommendation.
Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark put on four and seven crowns to finish at 636 and 361 respectively.
Tele Danmark rose another four crowns to 339 on lingering, unsubstantiated rumours of a possible BT bid for a stake in the tele-operator, while Novo Nordisk went up 12 crowns to 722.
